correctness.rationale: Each pair overlap has the exact hypergeometric law. Conditioning on all species sets except a leaf of any species-edge forest shows the leaf overlap is independent of all remaining edge overlaps; induction proves mutual factorization. Two distinct unordered edges form a forest, so all off-diagonal covariances of checkerboard pair contributions vanish. Exact factorial-moment multiplication derives the stated variance formula for all finite H≥2 and all prescribed row occupancies. Independent exact enumeration checks 649 marginal parameter pairs and 30,665 complete matrices, including shared-edge pair independence and a three-edge path. A three-singleton/two-site triangle disproves unrestricted joint independence. Computation is corroboration, not the proof.

evidence: Gotelli (2000) full article: Table 1 defines C-score as mean pairwise checkerboard units; Table 2 specifies SIM2 as fixed row sums and equiprobable columns; methods repeatedly randomize matrices (usually 1000 times) to obtain the null statistic distribution.
Veech (2013) full methodological section: exact probabilistic model covers selected species pairs under equal site probabilities and fixed species occupancy.
Arita (2016) full text discusses both pairwise and aggregate indices and exact Fisher/FE equivalence, including expected values and variances of pairwise overlap quantities in related analyses.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broad sources establish the sampling model and pairwise marginals, and Arita links the two levels. None inspected states that all edges in any forest give mutually independent overlaps or supplies the derived formula for the variance of the average of **all** pairwise checkerboard terms. Knowing marginals alone does not imply covariances vanish.

evidence: Arita (2016) explicitly recognizes that the standard per-pair law coincides with row-fixed/equiprobable-column randomization and that global statistics aggregate pair scores.
Veech (2013) proves only the marginal two-species probability distribution, which cannot alone determine an average-score variance.

The accepted theorem adds a forest-wise **joint** probability factorization and uses it to eliminate all covariance terms for arbitrary heterogeneous occupancies. Triangle cycles provide a precise boundary to stronger joint-independence claims.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior statements are not equivalent to the accepted multi-pair independence lemma or the variance formula. Marginal single-edge hypergeometric moments imply mean but not variance of a sum without dependency information. Leaf conditioning proves the essential extra cross-pair independence; the resulting formula is nonasymptotic and holds at all finite matrix sizes.

evidence: No inspected primary source included a table or analytic formula for the variance of the whole-matrix checkerboard C-score across the complete fixed-equiprobable null ensemble.
Some software defines c_score_var as the variance across pairwise checkerboard scores of one given matrix; this is a different quantity from variance across randomized complete matrices.

The exact small example with five sites and row sizes (2,3,4) yields whole-matrix null mean 7/5 and variance 49/75; its values are generated from the symbolic result and independently from 500 full matrices.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A published table of per-pair overlap variances or within-matrix pair-score dispersion does not imply an across-matrix variance of the pair-score average, because the latter includes cross-edge covariance contributions unless their vanishing is proved. No exact-table coverage was found.

originality.rationale: The found primary literature gives the C-score statistic, fixed--equiprobable row randomization, and exact marginal two-species hypergeometric probabilities; it does not derive a forest-indexed joint product distribution or a variance formula for the complete across-random-matrices C-score average. Arita (2016) is the closest potential implication: it connects pairwise Fisher tests with matrix-level aggregation but does not prove the off-diagonal terms vanish. The new conditional-leaf lemma is the substantive added premise required for that exact null variance. Exact searches found no covering result, with residual risk from broader random-set or U-statistic literature.
residual_risks: An equivalent forest-factorization or canonical degenerate-U-statistic argument may exist in more general combinatorial probability literature under a different name.
The original Stone--Roberts 1990 article was not read in full, although its exact statistic was inspected in the full Gotelli 2000 primary paper.
Exact null moments do not determine non-Gaussian tail probabilities, and the result is not applicable to fixed-column models or to heterogeneous habitat suitability.

value.rationale: The classical C-score is widely used to summarize ecological co-occurrence, and Gotelli (2000) evaluates it under SIM2 with repeated randomization. The accepted theorem gives exact finite mean and matrix-null variance for any heterogeneous row totals without Monte Carlo uncertainty or enumerating the full null space. Crucially, pairwise overlap marginals alone cannot yield the variance of an aggregate; the forest proof supplies the missing zero-covariance result, while the triangle obstruction prevents an erroneous complete independence or normality conclusion. The formula is directly useful for variance-based calibration under the precisely stated null.
